horizon_driver: Highly heterogeneous within the merged actor: national election cycles and external-debt rollover walls set a short clock for Turkey/Brazil/South Africa-type members, while GCC currency pegs operate on a multi-decade, non-electoral horizon. Treat the merged discount rate as an average masking wide internal variance.

capabilities.meaning: maintain current rate stance and FX regime
incremental reserve-composition adjustment or smoothing intervention
aggressive capital controls, a large one-off devaluation, or a sharp discrete reserve-composition shift

constraints.source: decades-long Saudi riyal / UAE dirham dollar pegs, defended as a fiscal-and-monetary-credibility anchor
constraints.breaks_under: never observed to break, including through prior oil-price collapses

constraints.source: varies sharply by member — Turkey's CBRT rate policy was repeatedly overridden by presidential pressure pre-2023, since partially restored; Brazil's BCB has held a more orthodox, credible line
constraints.breaks_under: an incumbent government facing an election within the discount horizon, most acutely in Turkey-type cases

constraints.source: gold and non-dollar asset purchases are themselves price-sensitive and constrained by the member's own FX-stability needs
constraints.breaks_under: not generally observed to break; diversification pace tracks each member's own reserve-adequacy comfort, not a coordinated bloc timetable

stated_vs_revealed.stated: A broad 'de-dollarization' narrative (BRICS-adjacent communications, national central bank statements) describes reserve diversification as a deliberate, coordinated, bloc-wide shift away from the dollar.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: IMF COFER data shows the US dollar's share of allocated global reserves moved only marginally, from 56.93% (2025Q3) to 56.77% (2025Q4), and independent analysis found that roughly 92% of a comparable 2025 decline was driven by currency valuation effects, not active central-bank portfolio reallocation. Real, deliberate gold accumulation is concentrated in a handful of outlier members — Turkey (28.4% of reserves in gold after adding 387 tonnes in 2022-24) — while others remain conservative: Brazil holds only about 2% of reserves in gold despite cutting its USD-asset share from 89% to ~78% over 2017-2024, and Indonesia holds under 4% in gold. Emerging-market central banks collectively raised their share of global official gold reserves from 18% (2000) to roughly 32% (end-2025), but this growth is uneven, not uniform across the bloc.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The bloc-wide 'de-dollarization' narrative substantially overstates a trend that is real only in specific outlier members and is mostly a slow, valuation-noisy process rather than a coordinated policy shift. Modeling this as one actor with one reserve-composition trajectory is itself a simplification the evidence argues against.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Members of this bloc broadly claim operational monetary-policy independence and market-driven exchange-rate regimes.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: GCC members maintain currency-board-style dollar pegs with no independent rate-setting at all; among the non-peg members, credibility varies widely — Turkey's central bank suppressed rates under direct political pressure pre-2023 while Brazil's has run a comparatively orthodox, credible inflation-targeting regime throughout the same period.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Claimed uniform 'independent inflation-targeting' status masks a very wide internal credibility spread. Any run that treats CB_EM's stated policy stance as a single signal should widen its uncertainty band accordingly, or split the actor when a run turns on one specific member (as the Cartographer's own notes elsewhere anticipate for other merged actors).

tripwires.if: global oil price falls sharply and stays below roughly $50/bbl
tripwires.then: GCC peg-defense costs rise materially, testing but historically not breaking the hard peg constraint

tripwires.if: a member's currency depreciates more than roughly 15% in a month
tripwires.then: capital controls escalate (Turkey-style precedent) regardless of stated free-float commitments

tripwires.if: gold prices correct more than roughly 20%
tripwires.then: EM gold-accumulation pace slows — buying is price-sensitive and opportunistic, not doctrinaire

what_would_change_my_mind: Sustained, multi-quarter, valuation-adjusted COFER evidence of a dollar-share decline concentrated across many (not just 2-3) EM central banks would upgrade the de-dollarization tripwire from 'narrative' to 'mechanism.' Flagged explicitly: this is a merged actor whose members (GCC pegs, Turkey, Brazil) behave too differently for a single utility function to be more than an approximation — the Orchestrator should widen the distribution on this actor specifically or consider splitting it if a run turns on any one member.
